title: Hospital audit study identifies limits of learned access explanations
summary: A hospital-field evaluation examined a machine-learning-based Explanation-Based Auditing System using staff access logs and scenario checks. The tool explained an average98.09% of accesses as appropriate; this measures explanation coverage, rather than breach-detection accuracy. Analysis linked many unexplained accesses to missing staff metadata and exceptional workflows, identifying limits that remained despite high overall coverage. This single-hospital evaluation does not establish fewer privacy breaches or generalizable detection performance.
ai_technology: Supervised learning in an Explanation-Based Auditing System (EBAS)
organization: University of Toronto; Mackenzie Richmond Hill Hospital

evidence.tested: Original paper abstract plus the author’s thesis chapter4, explicitly identified as the same2020 article, document a2017–2018 hospital study.13 clinical/non-clinical staff were selected for review, with additional constructed appropriate/inappropriate scenarios and longitudinal audit-output analysis. A seven-day analysis linked most unexplained accesses to absent role/department metadata.
evidence.unknown: Article full text was not retrieved; detailed Methods were checked in the author’s later thesis, not silently treated as the publisher version. Tool internals were black-box and the source does not expose a reproducible trained-model architecture. Coverage is not sensitivity, specificity or accuracy against comprehensive breach ground truth. One hospital and partly constructed scenarios; no measured breach reduction.
evidence.ai_role: The thesis identifies EBAS as a supervised-learning tool that combines electronic records and staff/scheduling data to generate learned access explanations; the study evaluates its outputs and operational failure patterns rather than training a new algorithm.

source_review.scope: Primary PubMed complete abstract and electronic publication date; author-deposited2022 doctoral thesis chapter4 original Methods and Results, including explicit relationship to the2020 article, EBAS identity, staff/scenario validation and unexplained-access analysis. Publisher full article remains unavailable.
